decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0.25% to 0.5%. The vote was 9-1. Dissenting: Esther L. George.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in June indicates that the labor market strengthened and that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate rate.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in April indicates that the pace of improvement in the labor market has slowed while growth in …”

changes.quote: Job gains were strong in June following weak growth in May.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: On balance, payrolls and other labor market indicators point to some increase in labor utilization in recent months.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Household spending has been growing strongly but business fixed investment has been soft.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Although the unemployment rate has declined, job gains have diminished.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: Growth in household spending has strengthened.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

tone_quotes.quote: The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting further improvement in labor market conditions and a return to 2 percent inflation.
This policy, by keeping the Committee's holdings of longer-term securities at sizable levels, should help maintain accommodative financial conditions.
Inflation has continued to run below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective, partly reflecting earlier declines in energy prices and in prices of non-energy imports.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.31% APR costs about $51.29 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.52% and moved -5 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.42% would fall by about $8.31 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.9%, and employers added an average of 162k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.1% over the past year (June 2016); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 1.3% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -2 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.14% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is balanced. The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 98%, cut 0%, hike 2%.

citations.detail: Against this backdrop, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1/4 to 1/2 percent.
